message.content:
**Traffic Laws in Texas – Quick Reference Guide** | Topic | Key Points | Where to Find More Info | |-------|------------|------------------------| | **Speed Limits** | • Posted limits apply unless otherwise indicated.
• 55 mph on rural interstates, 65 mph on urban interstates.
• 45 mph on most rural highways, 35 mph on many urban highways.
• 25 mph in school zones during school hours. | Texas Department of Transportation (TxDOT) – Speed Limit Regulations | | **Seat‑Belt & Child Restraint** | • All occupants must wear seat belts.
• Children under 8 years or 4 ft 9 in tall must use a child safety seat.
• Rear‑seat child restraints are required until age 13 or 4 ft 9 in. | TxDOT – Seat Belt and Child Restraint Laws | | **DUI / Alcohol** | • Blood alcohol concentration (BAC) of 0.08 % or higher is illegal for drivers over 21.
• Zero‑tolerance for drivers under 21 (BAC ≥ 0.02 %).
• Penalties include fines, license suspension, mandatory alcohol education, and possible jail time. | Texas Alcoholic Beverage Commission (TABC) – DUI Enforcement | | **Texting & Phone Use** | • Hand‑held phone use while driving is prohibited.
• Hands‑free devices are allowed but drivers must keep hands on wheel. | TxDOT – Mobile Phone Use Laws | | **Right‑of‑Way** | • Stop at stop signs; yield at yield signs.
• At uncontrolled intersections, yield to vehicles on the right.
• Pedestrians have priority at crosswalks. | TxDOT – Right‑of‑Way Rules | | **Lane Discipline** | • Keep left lane for passing; stay in right lane when not passing.
• Use turn lanes when turning. | TxDOT – Lane Discipline Guidelines | | **School Bus** | • Stop 20 ft from a school bus with flashing lights.
• Do not pass a stopped school bus until lights are off. | TxDOT – School Bus Safety | | **Parking** | • No parking within 20 ft of a fire hydrant.
• No parking in front of a driveway or on a sidewalk. | TxDOT – Parking Regulations | | **Vehicle Registration & Inspection** | • Vehicles must be registered and display valid license plates.
• Most vehicles require an annual safety inspection. | Texas Department of Motor Vehicles (TxDMV) – Vehicle Registration & Inspection | | **Insurance** | • Minimum liability coverage: $30,000 bodily injury per person, $60,000 per accident, $25,000 property damage. | TxDMV – Insurance Requirements | | **Special Situations** | • “No‑Stop” zones, construction zones, and temporary speed limits are enforced with signage.
• Rural roads may have “no‑stop” or “no‑passing” signs. | TxDOT – Road Signage Standards | --- ### How to Stay Updated 1. **Texas Transportation Code** – The official legal text governing all traffic laws. *Website:* https://statutes.capitol.texas.gov/Docs/TX/htm/TX.HTM 2. **TxDOT Traffic Safety Division** – Offers educational materials, statistics, and updates on enforcement. *Website:* https://www.txdot.gov/traffic-safety.html 3. **TxDMV** – Handles registration, insurance verification, and driver licensing. *Website:* https://www.txdmv.gov/ 4. **Local County Courts** – For specific case law or recent rulings affecting traffic regulations. --- ### Quick Tips for Safe Driving in Texas - **Always obey posted speed limits** – they’re set for safety and vary by road type. - **Use seat belts and child restraints** – it’s a legal requirement and saves lives. - **Avoid distractions** – keep your phone out of reach unless using a hands‑free system. - **Stay alert for school buses and construction zones** – they often have special rules. - **Keep your vehicle in good condition** – regular inspections help avoid violations. Feel free to let me know if you need deeper details on any specific law or how to handle a particular situation!
